topic: First Aid - Chopping Cut & Turmeric Application (చేయి కట్ అయినప్పుడు)
title: Chopping Cut & Turmeric First Aid Protocol
description: When a chef or kitchen staff cuts their finger/hand while chopping (చేయి కట్ అయ్యింది): 1. Immediately rinse the wound under cold running tap water to wash away dirt. 2. Apply pressure with a clean sterile cloth to stop bleeding. 3. Apply clean organic Turmeric powder (పసుపు) or antiseptic cream as a traditional antibacterial first-aid antiseptic to prevent infection and stop minor bleeding. 4. Wrap with a waterproof bandage or finger cot. 5. Crucial: The staff member must wear a glove before returning to food prep, or be reassigned away from direct food contact to ensure 100% food hygiene.
rule: Wash cut under cold running water, apply pressure, apply organic turmeric (పసుపు) or antiseptic cream, wrap with waterproof bandage, wear a glove before returning to food prep.

topic: First Aid - Hot Oil & Steam Burns (నూనె / ఆవిరి కాలడం)
title: Hot Oil & Steam Burn First Aid
description: For hot oil splashes or steam burns: 1. Cool the burned area immediately under cool running water for at least 10 to 15 minutes. 2. Do NOT apply ice directly or pop blisters. 3. Apply aloe vera gel or burn ointment. 4. Seek medical attention for deep or large burns.
rule: Cool under running water for 15 mins. Never apply ice directly. Use burn gel.

topic: First Aid - Slippery Floor & Falls (జారుడు నేల)
title: Slips, Trips & Wet Floor Safety
description: To prevent slips and falls: 1. Immediately wipe any oil, water, or sauce spills on the floor. 2. Place yellow 'Caution: Wet Floor' warning signs. 3. All kitchen staff must wear certified non-slip rubber-soled footwear.
rule: Clean spills immediately, use wet floor sign, wear non-slip shoes.

topic: Emergency - Commercial Gas Leak Protocol (గ్యాస్ లీక్ అయితే)
title: LPG Gas Leakage Emergency Response
description: If gas smell or LPG leak is detected (గ్యాస్ లీక్ అయ్యింది): 1. Immediately turn off the main gas regulator valve knob. 2. Open all doors and windows to vent gas. 3. DO NOT touch any electrical switches, exhaust fans, or light buttons. 4. Evacuate kitchen staff. 5. Call Deccan Commercial LPG Gas emergency helpline immediately.
rule: Turn off main regulator knob, open doors/windows, do NOT touch electrical switches, evacuate, call emergency gas hotline.

topic: Leftover Used Cooking Oil Management (మిగిలిన నూనె ఏమి చేయాలి)
title: Used Oil Storage & Disposal Rules
description: Handling leftover frying oil (నూనె మిగిలితే): 1. Allow oil to cool completely before handling. 2. Filter out burnt food crumbs through a fine mesh strainer into a clean stainless steel container. 3. Never reuse oil more than 2-3 times to prevent toxic trans-fats. 4. NEVER pour used oil down kitchen sink drains (it solidifies and blocks plumbing). 5. Store used oil in sealed drums for biodiesel recycling collection.
rule: Cool & strain oil into clean container. Max 2-3 reuses. Never pour oil down sink drains.

topic: Emergency - Hot Oil Fire (నూనె మంట పడితే)
title: Oil & Grease Fire Emergency Action
description: If hot oil catches fire in a pan or fryer (నూనెలో మంటలు వచ్చాయి): 1. NEVER EVER pour water on an oil fire! Water explodes hot oil into massive fireballs. 2. Turn off the burner stove heat source immediately. 3. Cover the pan with a tight-fitting metal lid, baking sheet, or damp heavy towel to smother flames. 4. Use a Class K or Class BC fire extinguisher if fire spreads.
rule: NEVER use water on oil fire. Turn off stove burner, smother pan with metal lid or damp towel.

topic: Food Spoilage & Bad Odor Check (ఫుడ్ పాడైతే / దుర్వాసన వస్తే)
title: Spoiled Food Inspection & Rejection
description: If meat, dairy, or cooked food smells sour, foul, or feels slimy (ఫుడ్ పాడైంది): 1. Immediately throw away spoiled items in outer waste bins. 2. NEVER taste questionable food to check spoilage. 3. Sanitize the storage shelf and container.
rule: If food smells sour/foul or feels slimy, discard immediately. Never taste suspect food.

topic: Cross Contamination Prevention (మాంసం కూరగాయలు కలవకుండా)
title: Raw Meat & Produce Separation
description: To prevent cross-contamination: 1. Use color-coded cutting boards (Red for Raw Meat, Green for Produce, Yellow for Poultry). 2. Store raw meat on the lowest shelf of the refrigerator below cooked food to prevent drippings. 3. Wash hands and knives after touching raw meat.
rule: Use color-coded cutting boards. Store raw meat on bottom fridge shelf below cooked food.

topic: Power Outage & Fridge Food Preservation (కరెంట్ పోయినప్పుడు)
title: Power Outage Refrigeration Protocol
description: During power cuts (కరెంట్ పోతే): 1. Keep refrigerator and walk-in cooler doors closed as much as possible. 2. Refrigerator keeps food cold for 4 hours if unopened. 3. Deep freezers keep food safe for 24-48 hours. 4. Discard perishable dairy/meat if fridge temp exceeds 10°C for over 4 hours.
rule: Keep fridge doors closed. Food stays safe for 4h in fridge, 24-48h in freezer.

topic: Emergency - Chemical Eye Splash (కెమికల్ కంట్లో పడితే)
title: Chemical Splash First Aid
description: If degreaser, bleach, or cleaning chemical splashes into eyes: 1. Rush to the eyewash station immediately. 2. Flush eyes with cold running water continuously for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. 3. Seek medical emergency attention.
rule: Flush eyes at eyewash sink for 15 mins continuously. Seek medical aid.

topic: Bulging & Dented Canned Food Check (డబ్బా పొంగితే)
title: Canned Goods Safety & Botulism Prevention
description: Inspect tin cans and canned ingredients: 1. Never open or use cans that are swollen, bulging, rusted, or severely dented. 2. Bulging cans indicate deadly Botulism toxin gas buildup. Discard immediately.
rule: Discard swollen, bulging, or dented cans immediately. Never open bulging cans.

topic: Broken Glass in Prep Counter (గాజు పగిలితే)
title: Broken Glass Cleanup & Food Isolation
description: If glass bottles or tableware break in food prep area (గాజు గ్లాస్ పగిలితే): 1. Halt prep work and isolate the area. 2. Throw away all exposed food, ice, or garnishes on nearby counters. 3. Sweep glass with broom and dustpan. 4. Wipe fine splinters with damp paper towel.
rule: Halt prep, throw away exposed food nearby, sweep glass, wipe splinters with damp paper towel.

topic: Mandoline Slicer & Cheese Grater Safety (తురుముతుంటే దెబ్బ తగలకుండా)
title: Slicer & Grater Safety Guard Rule
description: When using mandoline slicers or cheese graters: 1. Always use the food safety hand guard / push block attachment. 2. Never push vegetables with bare fingers when approaching blade end.
rule: Always use safety hand guard push block on mandoline slicers and graters.

topic: Pest Control & Pantry Contamination (పందికొక్కు/బొద్దింకలు కనిపిస్తే)
title: Pest Sighting & Pantry Protection
description: If pests or insects are sighted in dry pantry: 1. Report to Shift Manager immediately. 2. Inspect flour/grain bags for nibble marks and discard contaminated bags. 3. Store all dry grains in sealed heavy plastic bins.
rule: Report pest sightings, discard nibbled bags, store grains in sealed plastic bins.

topic: Deep Fryer Splatter Prevention (నూనె చిట్లకుండా ఉండటానికి)
title: Moisture & Oil Splatter Prevention
description: Before dropping raw chicken, paneer, or french fries into hot oil: 1. Thoroughly pat food dry with paper towels to remove surface water. 2. Ice or water droplets cause explosive hot oil splattering.
rule: Pat food dry before frying. Never drop wet or icy items into hot oil.

topic: Hot Cookware Handling (వేడి బాండీలు పట్టుకునేటప్పుడు)
title: Hot Pan & Oven Mitt Rule
description: When moving hot kadais, pans, or baking trays: 1. ALWAYS use thick DRY oven mitts or dry towels. 2. NEVER use a wet kitchen towel—water conducts heat instantly and creates severe steam burns on hands.
rule: Always use DRY oven mitts. Never use wet towels to lift hot pans.

topic: Raw Poultry Washing Safety (పచ్చి చికెన్ నీళ్ళలో కడగవచ్చా)
title: Raw Chicken Washing Contamination Warning
description: Rinsing raw chicken under tap water (పచ్చి చికెన్ కడగవచ్చా): 1. DO NOT wash raw chicken under running sink water. Water droplets splash Salmonella bacteria up to 3 feet onto counters and clean dishes. 2. Pat raw chicken dry with paper towels directly before cooking.
rule: Do NOT wash raw chicken under running sink tap. Pat dry with paper towels directly.

topic: Microwave Metal & Foil Spark Hazard (మైక్రోవేవ్‌లో స్టీల్ గిన్నె పెట్టవచ్చా)
title: Microwave Metal Safety
description: Using containers in microwave oven: 1. NEVER place stainless steel bowls, metal utensils, or aluminum foil inside microwave. 2. Metal causes electric arcing, sparks, and microwave fires. Use microwave-safe glass or ceramic only.
rule: Never put metal or aluminum foil in microwave. Use microwave-safe glass/ceramic only.

topic: Raw Egg Freshness Float Test (గుడ్డు మంచందో పాడైందో ఎలా తెలవాలి)
title: Egg Freshness Water Float Test
description: Testing if raw eggs are fresh or rotten (గుడ్డు టెస్టింగ్): 1. Place raw egg in a bowl of cold water. 2. Fresh eggs sink flat to the bottom. 3. Spoiled rotten eggs float to the top due to gas buildup (discard floating eggs immediately).
rule: Fresh eggs sink to bottom; rotten eggs float to top in water test.

topic: Blender Hot Liquid Venting (మిక్సీలో వేడి సూప్ గ్రైండ్ చేస్తే)
title: Blending Hot Soups & Liquids
description: Blending hot soup or hot sauces in blender/mixer: 1. Never fill blender container over halfway with hot liquid. 2. Remove center cap on lid to vent steam pressure. 3. Cover lid opening with folded towel before blending at low speed to prevent steam explosion.
rule: Fill blender max halfway with hot liquids, remove lid center cap to vent steam, cover with towel.

topic: Falling Knife Safety Rule (కత్తి కింద పడుతుంటే)
title: Falling Knife Safety Reaction
description: If a sharp knife slips and falls from counter: 1. NEVER attempt to catch a falling knife in mid-air! 2. Step back immediately, pull feet away, and let it fall to the floor. 3. Sanitize blade before picking up.
rule: A falling knife has no handle! Never catch a falling knife—step back immediately.

topic: Re-freezing Thawed Meat Warning (కరిగించిన చికెన్‌ని మళ్లీ ఫ్రీజ్ చేయవచ్చా)
title: Thawed Raw Meat Re-freezing Warning
description: Handling thawed frozen meat: 1. Never re-freeze raw meat that has been fully thawed at room temperature. 2. Re-freezing encourages rapid bacterial growth and ruins meat texture. Cook thawed meat immediately.
rule: Never re-freeze raw meat thawed at room temp. Cook thawed meat immediately.

topic: Overcrowding Frying Pan (ఫ్రై చేసేటప్పుడు గిన్నెలో ఎక్కువ వేస్తే)
title: Frying Pan Loading Rule
description: Frying food in batches: 1. Do not overcrowd deep fryers or frying pans. 2. Overcrowding drops oil temperature rapidly, causing food to absorb excess oil and become soggy instead of crispy.
rule: Fry in small batches. Overcrowding drops oil temp and makes food soggy.

topic: Thawing Frozen Meat Safely (ఫ్రోజెన్ చికెన్ డీఫ్రాస్ట్ ఎలా చేయాలి)
title: Safe Defrosting Protocols
description: Safely thawing frozen poultry/meat: 1. Thaw in refrigerator bottom shelf overnight (best method). 2. Submerge sealed meat pack in cold water bath changed every 30 mins. 3. Never leave frozen meat thawing on warm counter room temp.
rule: Thaw in fridge overnight or cold water bath. Never leave thawing on warm counter.

topic: Mold on Bread & Bakery Items (బ్రెడ్ మీద మచ్చలు/నాచు వస్తే)
title: Bakery Mold Safety
description: If mold spots appear on bread slice or soft bakery items: 1. Discard the ENTIRE loaf or package immediately. 2. Mold roots spread unseen microscopic toxins throughout porous bread. Do not just cut off green spots.
rule: Discard entire bread loaf if mold appears. Mold roots spread deep through porous bread.

topic: Cooked Rice Storage & Spoilage Toxin (అన్నం బయట ఉంచితే ఏమవుతుంది)
title: Bacillus Cereus Rice Poisoning Prevention
description: Handling cooked rice: 1. Never leave cooked rice at room temperature for over 2 hours. 2. Room temp rice breeds Bacillus cereus bacteria toxins that survive reheating. 3. Cool rice quickly and store in fridge within 1 hour.
rule: Never leave cooked rice at room temp >2 hours. Refrigerate within 1 hour.

topic: Cutting Board Sanitization (కటింగ్ బోర్డ్ కడగడం ఎలా)
title: Cutting Board Washing & Sanitizing
description: Sanitizing cutting boards after use: 1. Wash cutting boards with hot soapy water. 2. Spray with food-safe sanitizer or diluted bleach water solution after cutting raw meat. 3. Air dry completely in vertical rack.
rule: Wash with hot soapy water, sanitize after raw meat, air dry vertically in rack.

topic: FIFO Stock Rotation Rule (పాత సరుకులు ముందు వాడటం)
title: First-In, First-Out (FIFO) Rotation
description: Managing pantry and cold storage inventory: 1. Always place new stock behind older stock on shelves. 2. Use older ingredients with earlier expiry dates first (FIFO). 3. Label all opened packages with date.
rule: Place new stock behind older stock. Use earlier expiry date items first (FIFO).

topic: Cooling Hot Soups & Curries (వేడి కూర/సూప్ ఫ్రిజ్‌లో పెట్టవచ్చా)
title: Rapid Cooling Protocols for Hot Food
description: Cooling hot large pots of gravy/soup before refrigeration: 1. Never put piping hot large pots directly into walk-in cooler (it raises cooler internal temp and spoils nearby food). 2. Divide hot food into shallow pans or use ice baths to cool to 21°C within 2 hours.
rule: Cool hot food in shallow pans or ice bath before placing in fridge. Never put piping hot pots in cooler.

topic: Kitchen Staff Hairnet & Hygiene Rule (జుట్టు పడకుండా)
title: Staff Personal Hygiene & Hair Restraints
description: Kitchen staff dress code: 1. All staff must wear clean hairnets or chef caps at all times in kitchen area. 2. Beard nets required for staff with facial hair. 3. Remove wristwatches and rings before prep.
rule: Wear hairnets/chef caps and beard covers at all times. Remove jewelry before prep.

topic: Handwashing 20-Second Rule (చేతులు ఎలా కడగాలి)
title: Standard BOH Handwashing Protocol
description: Washing hands in kitchen: 1. Wash hands with warm running water and antibacterial soap for at least 20 seconds. 2. Wash before starting prep, after handling raw meat, after garbage handling, and after bathroom breaks.
rule: Scrub hands with soap and warm water for 20 seconds before prep and after raw meat/trash.

topic: Broken Plate & Glass Disposal Safety (పగిలిన ప్లేట్లు ఎక్కడ వేయాలి)
title: Sharp Glass & Ceramic Disposal Rule
description: Disposing of broken crockery, glass, or ceramics: 1. Wrap broken sharp pieces in thick cardboard or heavy paper box. 2. Label container 'SHARP GLASS' before tossing into trash to protect cleaning staff from cuts.
rule: Wrap sharp broken glass/crockery in cardboard before trash disposal. Label 'SHARP GLASS'.

topic: Exhaust Hood Filter Cleaning (పొగగొట్టం నూనె జిడ్డు శుభ్రం)
title: Exhaust Hood Grease Filter Maintenance
description: Kitchen hood filter maintenance: 1. Clean exhaust hood grease filters weekly with degreaser chemical. 2. Accumulated grease in hood ducting is the #1 cause of commercial kitchen range fires.
rule: Clean hood grease filters weekly. Accumulated duct grease causes commercial kitchen fires.

topic: Electrical Safety & Wet Hands (తడి చేతులతో స్విచ్ వేస్తే)
title: Wet Hands Electrical Shock Prevention
description: Operating electrical equipment: 1. NEVER touch electrical switches, plugs, blenders, or mixers with wet hands. 2. Thoroughly dry hands before operating kitchen electrical appliances to avoid severe electrical shocks.
rule: Never touch electrical switches, plugs, or mixers with wet hands. Dry hands thoroughly first.

topic: Pressure Cooker Safety & Steam Release (కుక్కర్ విజిల్ మూత తీసేటప్పుడు)
title: Pressure Cooker Steam Safety
description: Opening pressure cookers safely: 1. Never force open a hot pressure cooker lid! 2. Wait until steam pressure releases fully and whistle weight drops down naturally, or run cool water over lid to cool down before opening.
rule: Never force open a hot pressure cooker. Wait for steam to vent fully before opening lid.

topic: First Aid - Choking & Heimlich Maneuver (ఎవరైనా ఊపిరి ఆడకపోతే)
title: Staff & Guest Choking First Aid
description: If someone is choking on food and cannot breathe or speak: 1. Perform Heimlich maneuver (stand behind victim, wrap arms around waist, make a fist above navel, give quick upward thrusts). 2. Call emergency medical team immediately.
rule: Perform Heimlich maneuver (upward abdominal thrusts from behind) for choking victims. Call emergency medical aid.

topic: Deep Fryer Water Splash Explosion (నూనెలో నీళ్ళు/ఐస్ పడితే)
title: Hot Oil Water Explosion Prevention
description: Preventing fryer explosions: 1. Never drop ice cubes, wet ingredients, or water into hot fryer oil. 2. Water vaporizes 1,700 times its volume instantly, causing explosive hot oil splatters and violent fires.
rule: Never drop ice or water into hot fryer oil. Water expands 1,700x as steam causing oil explosions.

topic: Heavy Ergonomic Lifting (బరువైన పెట్టెలు మూటలు ఎత్తేటప్పుడు)
title: Ergonomic Back Injury Prevention
description: Lifting heavy rice/flour bags and oil cans: 1. Bend knees and lift with leg muscles, keeping back straight. 2. Never lift heavy loads by bending back. 3. Store heavy items on middle shelves between waist and knee height.
rule: Bend knees and lift heavy bags with legs, not back. Keep heavy items on waist-height shelves.

topic: Food Allergy Cross-Contact Prevention (అలర్జీ ఫుడ్ చేసేటప్పుడు)
title: Allergen Cross-Contact Prevention
description: Preparing allergen-free orders (peanut, gluten, dairy allergies): 1. Use clean sanitized pans, knives, and cutting boards. 2. Never use spoons contaminated with nuts, flour, or milk in allergen-free orders.
rule: Use clean sanitized pans and utensils for allergen orders. Never cross-contaminate with nuts/dairy.

topic: Wet Plate Stacking & Mold Mildew Risk (తడి పళ్ళాలు అమరిస్తే)
title: Crockery Air Drying Protocol
description: Storing washed plates and bowls: 1. Never stack wet plates flat on top of each other. 2. Trapped moisture breeds foul mildew odors and bacterial slime. Air dry vertically in dish racks before stacking.
rule: Air dry plates vertically in dish racks before stacking. Never stack wet crockery flat.

topic: Internal Cooking Temperature Probe (మాంసం ఎంతవరకు ఉడకాలి)
title: Internal Food Cooking Temperatures
description: Checking cooked meat safety with food thermometer: 1. Poultry/Chicken: 74°C (165°F). 2. Minced/Ground Meat: 71°C (160°F). 3. Whole Mutton/Beef Steaks: 63°C (145°F). 4. Insert thermometer into thickest part of meat.
rule: Cook poultry to 74°C (165°F), minced meat to 71°C (160°F), mutton/steaks to 63°C (145°F).

topic: Raw Sprouts Bacteria Warning (పచ్చి మొలకలు అలా తినవచ్చా)
title: Raw Sprouts Cooking Requirement
description: Serving bean sprouts and sprouted moong: 1. Always steam or blanch raw sprouts before serving in salads or gravies. 2. Warm moist sprouting conditions breed dangerous E. coli and Salmonella bacteria.
rule: Always steam or blanch raw sprouts before serving to kill Salmonella and E. coli.

topic: Slicing Round Vegetables Safely (గుండ్రటి కూరగాయలు కోసేటప్పుడు)
title: Stable Base Cutting Technique
description: Cutting round tomatoes, potatoes, or onions: 1. Slice round vegetables in half first to create a flat, non-slip base on the cutting board. 2. Cutting round wobbly vegetables leads to knife slippage cuts.
rule: Cut round vegetables in half first to create a flat stable base on cutting board.

topic: Ice Machine Sanitation & Glass Scoop Hazard (ఐస్ చేతితో లేదా గ్లాస్‌తో తీస్తే)
title: Ice Machine Hygiene & Scoop Rules
description: Handling ice cubes in ice machine: 1. Never scoop ice using drinking glassware (glass can chip into ice unnoticed). 2. Never use bare hands. 3. Always use designated plastic ice scoop stored in clean holder.
rule: Never scoop ice with drinking glass or bare hands. Always use plastic ice scoop.

topic: Raw Honey Infant Botulism Warning (పిల్లలకు పచ్చి తేనె ఇవ్వవచ్చా)
title: Raw Honey Age Restriction
description: Serving raw honey in dishes or desserts: 1. NEVER serve raw honey to infants under 1 year of age. 2. Raw honey contains Clostridium botulinum spores that cause fatal infant botulism poisoning.
rule: Never serve raw honey to infants under 1 year old (infant botulism risk).

topic: Overheating Teflon Non-Stick Pans (నాన్-స్టిక్ పెనం ఎక్కువ వేడి చేస్తే)
title: Teflon Non-Stick Pan Overheating Warning
description: Using non-stick cookware: 1. Never heat empty Teflon non-stick pans on high heat flame over 260°C. 2. Overheated Teflon coating releases toxic polymer fumes that cause flu-like symptoms.
rule: Never heat empty non-stick Teflon pans on high heat (prevents toxic PTFE fume release).

topic: Raw Fish Parasite Freeze Rule (సషీమి పచ్చి చేపల్లో పురుగులు)
title: Raw Fish Parasite Destruction Protocol
description: Serving raw fish or sushi/sashimi dishes: 1. Freeze raw fish at -20°C (-4°F) for at least 7 days before raw service. 2. Commercial freezing destroys harmful Anisakis parasite larvae.
rule: Freeze raw fish intended for raw consumption at -20°C for 7 days to kill parasites.

topic: Chef Handwashing Frequency & Protocol (చాయ్ / చెఫ్ ఎన్ని సార్లు హ్యాండ్‌వాష్ చేసుకోవాలి / cheff enni sarlu handwash chesukuntadu)
title: Chef Handwashing Frequency & Hygiene Standard
description: Chef handwashing rules: 1. Wash hands every 30 minutes, after handling raw meat/poultry, after touching face/hair, after trash handling, after restroom use, and before starting any food prep. 2. Scrub with warm water and soap for at least 20 seconds. 3. Dry with single-use paper towels or air dryer.
rule: Wash hands every 30 minutes and after raw meat/restroom/trash contact for 20 seconds.

topic: Hair Net & Beard Cover Protocol (హెయిర్ నెట్ వేసుకోవాలా / hair net mandatory ah)
title: BOH Hair Constraint & Beard Restraint Standard
description: Hair and beard hygiene: 1. Hair nets and beard covers are mandatory in all food prep and cooking stations. 2. Keeps loose hair from contaminating dishes and maintains 100% kitchen cleanliness.
rule: Hair nets and beard covers must be worn at all times in food prep areas.

topic: Nail Trimming & Polish Ban (గోళ్లు కట్ చేయాలా / gollu cut cheyyala)
title: Chef Nail Care & Polish Prohibition
description: Hand nail hygiene: 1. Keep fingernails short, clean, and neatly trimmed. 2. Nail polish and artificial fingernails are strictly prohibited because chipped polish or false nails can drop into food.
rule: Keep nails short and unpolished; artificial nails prohibited in kitchen.

topic: Jewelry & Ring Policy in BOH (రింగులు గొలుసులు వేసుకోవచ్చా / rings jewelry veskovacha)
title: BOH Jewelry Restriction Standard
description: Kitchen jewelry rules: 1. No watches, bracelets, stone rings, or loose jewelry allowed in BOH stations. 2. Only a plain smooth metal wedding band is permitted. 3. Prevents physical hazards and bacterial harborage.
rule: Remove all jewelry except plain smooth wedding band before food prep.

topic: Chef Uniform & Clean Apron Change (ఏప్రాన్ ఎప్పుడు మార్చాలి / apron enni sarlu marchali)
title: Clean Apron & Uniform Hygiene Protocol
description: Apron and uniform maintenance: 1. Wear clean uniform daily. 2. Change aprons immediately when soiled with raw meat juices. 3. ALWAYS remove aprons before entering restrooms or taking out trash to prevent cross-contamination.
rule: Remove aprons before using restroom or trash disposal; change soiled aprons.

topic: Sickness & Open Wound Reporting (జ్వరం వికారంగా ఉంటే కిచెన్‌లో పనిచేయవచ్చా / sickness jwaram osthe)
title: Staff Illness Exclusion & Wound Cover Protocol
description: Kitchen staff sickness policy: 1. Staff with fever, diarrhea, vomiting, or jaundice must report to manager immediately and be excluded from food prep. 2. Cuts on hands must be covered with waterproof blue bandage and single-use glove.
rule: Exclude sick staff from kitchen; cover hand cuts with waterproof bandage and glove.

topic: Cutting Board Color Coding (కటింగ్ బోర్డు రంగులు దేనికి / red blue yellow board difference)
title: Color-Coded Cutting Board Standard
description: Cutting board color rules: 1. Red: Raw Red Meat. 2. Yellow: Raw Poultry (Chicken). 3. Blue: Raw Fish & Seafood. 4. Green: Fruits & Vegetables. 5. White: Dairy, Cheese & Bread. 6. Brown: Cooked Meats.
rule: Use color-coded cutting boards to prevent raw and ready-to-eat cross-contamination.

topic: Sanitizer Bucket PPM Concentration (శానిటైజర్ లిక్విడ్ వాటర్ ఎంత కలపాలి / sanitizer bucket ratio)
title: Prep Station Sanitizer Bucket Concentration Protocol
description: Sanitizing solution maintenance: 1. Maintain Chlorine sanitizer at 50-100 PPM (or Quat at 200 PPM). 2. Test concentration with test strips every 2-4 hours. 3. Replace sanitizer solution when greasy or diluted.
rule: Check sanitizer PPM concentration with test strips every 2-4 hours.

topic: Walk-in Fridge Temperature Standard (ఫ్రిజ్ టెంపరేచర్ ఎంత ఉండాలి / fridge temperature enni degrees)
title: Refrigeration & Walk-in Cooler Temperature Control
description: Cold storage temperatures: 1. Walk-in fridge and chillers must be kept at 1°C to 4°C (34°F to 40°F). 2. Freezers must be kept at -18°C (0°F) or colder. 3. Log temperatures twice daily.
rule: Maintain chillers between 1°C-4°C and freezers at -18°C or colder.

topic: Hot Holding Temperature Threshold (వేడి వంటలు ఎంత వేడిగా ఉండాలి / hot food temperature threshold)
title: BOH Hot Holding & Buffet Temperature Protocol
description: Hot food holding: 1. Maintain cooked hot foods at 60°C (140°F) or hotter in bain-maries. 2. Check internal temperature using calibrated probe thermometer every 2 hours.
rule: Hold cooked foods at 60°C (140°F) or hotter to prevent bacterial growth.

topic: Danger Zone Temperature Range (డేంజర్ జోన్ టెంపరేచర్ అంటే ఏంటి / temperature danger zone)
title: Foodborne Bacteria Temperature Danger Zone
description: Temperature Danger Zone rules: 1. Danger Zone is 5°C to 60°C (41°F to 140°F) where bacteria multiply rapidly. 2. Perishable food left in Danger Zone for >2 hours must be discarded.
rule: Keep cold foods below 5°C and hot foods above 60°C; limit Danger Zone time to 2 hours.

topic: Two-Stage Cooling Process for Stocks & Curries (వేడి కర్రీలు త్వరగా ఎలా చల్లార్చాలి / cooling hot curry)
title: BOH Two-Stage Rapid Food Cooling Protocol
description: Cooling hot curries and gravies: 1. Stage 1: Cool from 60°C to 21°C within 2 hours. 2. Stage 2: Cool from 21°C to 5°C within next 4 hours. 3. Use ice baths, ice paddles, or shallow metal pans.
rule: Cool hot foods from 60°C to 21°C in 2 hrs, then 21°C to 5°C in 4 hrs using ice baths.

topic: Thawing Meat Rules (మాంసం ఐస్ కరిగించడానికి గదిలో పెట్టవచ్చా / thawing meat ice melt)
title: Safe Frozen Meat Thawing Methods
description: Safe thawing techniques: 1. In refrigerator below 4°C (recommended). 2. Submerged under cold running water below 21°C. 3. Microwave (only if cooking immediately). 4. NEVER thaw meat at room temperature.
rule: Never thaw frozen meat at room temperature; use refrigerator or cold running water.

topic: Food Labeling & Expiry Sticker Rule (ప్రిపేర్ చేసిన ఫుడ్ పైన డేట్ లేబుల్ వేయాలా / food labeling date sticker)
title: BOH Prep Labeling & Expiry Tracking Standard
description: Food labeling procedure: 1. All prepped sauces, sliced meats, and chopped veggies must have Date Labels. 2. Label must include: Item Name, Prep Date, Time, Use-By Expiry Date, and Chef Initials.
rule: Label all prepped items with Item Name, Prep Date/Time, Expiry Date, and Initials.

topic: FIFO Storage Protocol (ఫిఫో సిస్టమ్ అంటే ఏంటి / fifo system rules)
title: First-In, First-Out (FIFO) Inventory Management
description: FIFO inventory rule: 1. Store new stock behind older stock. 2. Use items with earlier expiration dates first. 3. Prevents ingredient spoilage and reduces kitchen food waste.
rule: Always use older stock first (First-In, First-Out) to prevent ingredient spoilage.

topic: Raw Meat Storage Hierarchy (చికెన్ మటన్ ఫ్రిజ్‌లో ఎక్కడ పెట్టాలి / raw meat fridge placement)
title: Refrigerator Shelf Storage Hierarchy
description: Fridge shelf arrangement (Top to Bottom): 1. Top Shelf: Ready-to-Eat Food / Cooked Dishes. 2. Middle Shelf: Raw Fish & Seafood. 3. Lower Shelf: Raw Whole Beef & Pork. 4. Bottom Shelf: Raw Chicken & Ground Meat.
rule: Store raw poultry and ground meats on the lowest fridge shelf below cooked foods.

topic: Tasting Food Hygiene Protocol (కర్రీల టేస్ట్ చూసేటప్పుడు / tasting spoon rule)
title: Sanitary Food Tasting Standard
description: Tasting dishes during cooking: 1. Ladle small portion into a separate clean tasting spoon or cup. 2. Step away from cooking pot to taste. 3. NEVER double-dip or reuse tasting spoon in cooking pot.
rule: Use a separate clean spoon for food tasting and never double-dip into cooking pot.

topic: Chemical Storage Segregation (క్లీనింగ్ లిక్విడ్స్ ఎక్కడ పెట్టాలి / chemical storage liquids)
title: BOH Chemical Storage & Isolation Standard
description: Storing cleaning chemicals: 1. Store detergents, bleach, and sanitizers in a locked chemical cabinet away from food prep areas. 2. NEVER store chemicals above food, plates, or single-use items.
rule: Store cleaning chemicals in dedicated locked cabinets separated from all food prep areas.

topic: Fly & Pest Control Screen Rule (కిచెన్‌లో ఈగలు బొద్దింకలు రాకుండా / fly pest control)
title: Pest Prevention & Air Curtain Protocol
description: Pest control guidelines: 1. Keep BOH back doors closed; maintain active air curtains and insect light traps. 2. Inspect incoming produce crates for pests before bringing into kitchen.
rule: Keep back doors closed, maintain air curtains, and inspect incoming crates for pests.

topic: Trash Can Foot-Pedal Rule (డస్ట్‌బిన్ చేతితో తెరవవచ్చా / dustbin foot pedal rule)
title: Waste Container Operation & Sanitization
description: Trash bin usage: 1. Kitchen waste bins must have working foot-pedals so staff never touch bin lids with hands. 2. Empty trash bins when 3/4 full. 3. Wash hands immediately after trash disposal.
rule: Use foot-pedal trash cans; wash hands immediately after touching waste containers.

topic: Mop Bucket & Broom Segregation (మాప్ బకెట్ ఎక్కడ కడగాలి / mop sink bucket wash)
title: Sanitation Equipment & Mop Sink Isolation
description: Washing mops and brooms: 1. Wash mops, buckets, and floor brooms exclusively in designated Mop Sinks (Service Sinks). 2. NEVER wash floor mops in food prep sinks or handwash sinks.
rule: Wash mops and buckets only in designated service mop sinks, never in food prep sinks.

topic: Exhaust Hood Filter Cleaning (ఎగ్జాస్ట్ హుడ్ ఎప్పుడు క్లీన్ చేయాలి / exhaust hood cleaning)
title: Grease Filter Maintenance & Fire Prevention
description: Exhaust hood maintenance: 1. Remove and degrease stainless steel hood filters weekly. 2. Prevents accumulated grease from dripping onto cooking griddles or catching fire.
rule: Degrease and clean exhaust hood filters weekly to prevent grease fires and dripping.

topic: Slicing Machine Sanitization Routine (మీట్ స్లైసర్ మెషిన్ ఎప్పుడు కడగాలి / meat slicer cleaning)
title: Commercial Slicer Cleaning & Disassembly Protocol
description: Meat slicer sanitization: 1. Unplug slicer, set blade depth to zero, disassemble blade guard and carriage. 2. Wash, rinse, and sanitize after every 4 hours of continuous use or between meat types.
rule: Unplug, disassemble, and sanitize meat slicers every 4 hours and when switching meat types.

topic: Dishwashing 3-Compartment Sink Routine (3 పార్ట్ సింక్ డిష్ వాషింగ్ / 3 compartment sink steps)
title: Manual Dishwashing 3-Compartment Sink Protocol
description: Manual dishwashing steps: 1. Sink 1: Wash in hot soapy water (minimum 43°C). 2. Sink 2: Rinse in clean warm water. 3. Sink 3: Sanitize in chemical solution for 60 seconds. 4. Air-dry completely.
rule: Wash (43°C), Rinse, Sanitize (60s), and Air-Dry all pots, pans, and utensils.

topic: Wiping Cloth Sanitizer Storage (తుడిచే తడి గుడ్డలు కౌంటర్‌పై పెట్టవచ్చా / wiping cloth sanitizer bucket)
title: Sanitizer Bucket Wiping Towel Protocol
description: Using wiping towels: 1. Damp wiping towels used for counters must be stored submerged in sanitizer buckets between uses. 2. NEVER leave damp wiping cloths sitting on prep counters.
rule: Keep damp wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer buckets when not actively wiping.

topic: Raw Egg Shell Wash Warning (గుడ్లను నీళ్లతో కడగవచ్చా / raw egg shell wash warning)
title: Shell Egg Storage & Handling Standard
description: Handling raw eggs: 1. Do NOT wash raw egg shells before storage (washing removes natural protective cuticle, letting bacteria enter). 2. Inspect for cracks and store refrigerated at <4°C.
rule: Do not wash raw shell eggs before storage; keep refrigerated below 4°C.

topic: Ice Machine Hygiene & Scoop Usage (ఐస్ స్కూప్ మెషిన్ లోపల పెట్టవచ్చా / ice scoop holder usage)
title: Ice Storage & Scoop Holder Standard
description: Ice machine safety: 1. Store ice scoop outside the ice machine bin in a clean, sanitized holder or bracket. 2. NEVER leave scoop handle sitting inside the ice. 3. Wash ice bin monthly.
rule: Store ice scoop outside ice bin in clean holder; never leave scoop handle inside ice.

topic: Food Spoilage Smell & Mold Rejection (చెడిపోయిన వాసన వస్తే ఉడికించవచ్చా / food spoilage mold smell)
title: Food Spoilage & Contamination Rejection Policy
description: Handling questionable food: 1. Discard any item showing off-odors, slime, discoloration, or mold immediately. 2. NEVER attempt to boil or cook spoiled food to save it (heat does not destroy all bacterial toxins).
rule: Discard spoiled or moldy food immediately; cooking does not destroy all bacterial toxins.

topic: Gloves Changing Frequency (గ్లోవ్స్ ఎప్పుడు మార్చాలి / gloves changing frequency)
title: Single-Use Disposable Glove Hygiene Standard
description: Glove replacement rules: 1. Change disposable gloves every 4 hours of continuous task, when torn, after touching face/hair/trash, or when switching from raw chicken to salad prep.
rule: Change single-use gloves every 4 hours, when torn, or when switching food prep tasks.

topic: Daily Closing BOH Sanitation Checklist (నైట్ కిచెన్ క్లోజింగ్ క్లీనింగ్ రొటీన్ / night closing kitchen checklist)
title: BOH Shift-End Closing Sanitation & Lockout Protocol
description: BOH night closing routine: 1. Sweep and mop all floors with floor sanitizer. 2. Sanitize stainless counters. 3. Drain dishwashing machine. 4. Empty all trash cans. 5. Turn off main LPG gas valve. 6. Lock walk-in coolers.
rule: Complete floor mopping, counter sanitization, trash emptying, and LPG gas lockout at closing.
